scope: Measure every entrypoint that exists locally, in a disposable network-isolated container, using subagents for parallel shards, and make the conclusion reproducible.

environment.python_system: 3.9.6 (below the documented requirement; the venv is used instead)
environment.docker_vm: Docker Desktop VM: 2 CPUs / 4095643648 bytes RAM
environment.critical_lesson: Every extra `docker` call competes with the browser for the VM's 2 CPUs. Polling with a throwaway container or `docker exec` turned 3.5 s per entry into minutes and was the real cause of the observed 4-17 minute stalls.

defects_fixed.what: `--collect` was rejected by the `--root is required` check before it could copy reports
defects_fixed.fix: validate --root/--entry only on the paths that need them

defects_fixed.what: detached batch containers kept `--rm`, so the container was deleted on exit and `docker cp` had nothing to read
the image ENTRYPOINT is python3, so a shell driver was handed to the Python interpreter (SyntaxError)
defects_fixed.fix: override the entrypoint for the batch driver

defects_fixed.what: parallel shards staged their manifest at the same path and overwrote each other

I rewrote the batch driver in shell to 'supervise Python from outside'. The rationale was wrong: run_batch already delegates supervision to an external `timeout -s KILL` and writes TIMEOUT_ABORTED. My fallback call omitted the required --root and discarded stderr, so 5 timeout reports were silently lost (109/114). A subagent found it by reporting that the report count did not match the manifest.
defects_fixed.fix: deleted my driver and reused the existing implementation (net less code); added the genuinely needed --detach/--collect/per-name staging; and finally TESTED the timeout path with a deliberately hanging fixture - the verification whose absence let the bug hide. Result: 14/14 reports present, including 4 TIMEOUT_ABORTED.

defects_fixed.what: the probe treated 'pixels changed after input' as input response, which a self-animating page satisfies without reacting to anything: 10 of 11 reported INPUT_RESPONSIVE entries were already changing during the idle baseline, and 7 had a byte-identical DOM from load to finish
defects_fixed.fix: new scripts/input_attribution.py, shared by both probes AND the offline aggregator, so historical reports are re-read with the corrected rule instead of being re-measured. The headline number went DOWN from 11 to 4, and the previous round's 4 included 2 that do not survive the rule.

defects_fixed.what: the survey aggregator counted 'probe saw a reaction' as gameplay_verified, while import_browser_report.py requires self-reported reports to declare gameplay_verified False
defects_fixed.fix: probes always write False; the survey artifact's gameplay_verified is always 0 (pinned by a test); input_responsive is the machine claim

defects_fixed.what: circular-tic-tac-toe landed in OTHER: 'Failed to read the serviceWorker property ... lacks the allow-same-origin flag' is the same root cause as shooter.html's localStorage error
defects_fixed.fix: classified as SANDBOX_OPAQUE_ORIGIN_BREAKS_OWN_SCRIPT; renderer crashes split out as RENDERER_CRASHED_ENVIRONMENT_LIMIT because on a 2 CPU / 4 GB VM that is an environment limit

defects_fixed.what: aaron-sulbaran/jester was reported missing_assets because three favicons were absent, while the game itself was fine
defects_fixed.fix: missing_static_assets() ignores icons/manifests/fonts, the same things the runtime probe stubs. jester's real cause is now measured (its own TS module fails CORS under the opaque origin), and phone-games' genuinely absent engine.js is still reported

defects_fixed.what: the catalog's sandbox_incompatible/runtime_* rows had no script that could produce them; only collect_repositories.py preserved them, so they were not auditable or reproducible
defects_fixed.fix: new scripts/apply_survey_to_catalog.py: fail-closed writer that only writes restrictive statuses, refuses surveys without isolation config/evidence, never weakens an existing conclusion, supports evidenced retraction, and records the evidence file's sha256

defects_fixed.what: browser_gameplay_probe.STATUSES did not list the new status after the rule changed
defects_fixed.fix: the vocabulary now uses the shared constants, so the rule and the vocabulary cannot drift apart
